mechanics.name: Better Than New
mechanics.currentEffect: Whenever you finish healing another Survivor, until they take damage, they Bless and Cleanse Totems, heal, and unlock Chests 40/45/50% faster.
activation: Ends/deactivates when: The affected Survivor loses the bonuses when they take damage.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (10.2.0): Increased the affected Survivor's Blessing/Cleansing, healing, and Chest-unlocking speed bonuses from 12/14/16% to 40/45/50%.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: Finishing a heal gives that Survivor faster Totem interactions, healing, and Chest unlocking until they take damage.
duration: Persists on the healed Survivor until they take damage.
specialInteractions: The bonuses apply to the Survivor you finished healing, not to you.

editorial.summary: After you finish healing someone, they heal, bless/cleanse, and unlock Chests up to 50% faster until they take damage.
useCases: Turn one completed heal into a strong support buff on that teammate.
Create a fast healer who can immediately help reset someone else.
Buff a teammate before they work through Hexes, Boons, or chest interactions.
counters: The buff disappears as soon as the affected Survivor takes damage.
It does not increase generator repair speed.
You must first complete a full heal on someone else.
pros: Up to 50% is a major support-speed bonus.
No cooldown after the initial heal trigger.
cons: Target loses everything on the next hit.
Value depends on the healed teammate actually using the supported actions.
analysis: Better Than New is one of the clearest 10.2 winners. The old 16% ceiling became 50% for healing, Totem interactions, and Chest unlocking, which is finally large enough to shape team decisions.
The best use is chaining support. Heal an injured teammate, then let that newly buffed Survivor perform the next heal dramatically faster while you return to another task.
The effect is fragile because one hit removes it, and generator repair is not part of the speed package. A Killer applying broad injury pressure can therefore erase value quickly.
Even with those limits, the old low-tier reputation is obsolete. The independent ranking review should treat the 10.2 version as a serious support perk rather than legacy filler.
editorial.verdict: A legitimate support perk after a huge 10.2 buff. Fifty percent faster healing and side-objective actions gives the healed Survivor something worth protecting.
